title: Fibonacci Modulo with Pisano Period
statement:
The Fibonacci numbers are defined by `F(0) = 0`, `F(1) = 1` and `F(i) = F(i - 1) + F(i - 2)` for `i ≥ 2`.

Given two integers `n` and `m`, compute `F(n) mod m`, the remainder when the `n`-th Fibonacci number is divided by `m`.

`n` can be as large as 10^15, so the number `F(n)` cannot be computed directly (it has more than 10^14 digits) and iterating `n` times is far too slow. The key fact is that the sequence `F(0) mod m, F(1) mod m, F(2) mod m, ...` is periodic. Its period is called the **Pisano period** of `m`, and it is at most `6m`.
inputFormat: A single line containing two integers `n` and `m`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: `F(n) mod m`.

examples.explanation: The Pisano period of 10 is 60 and 10^12 mod 60 = 40, so the answer is F(40) mod 10 = 102334155 mod 10 = 5.
Every number leaves remainder 0 when divided by 1.

hints: Only the remainders matter: the pair (F(i) mod m, F(i+1) mod m) determines everything after it, and there are only m^2 possible pairs, so the sequence must eventually repeat.
The sequence of remainders always returns to the starting pair (0, 1). Generate remainders until you see the pair (0, 1) again; the number of steps is the Pisano period p (p ≤ 6m).
Then F(n) mod m = F(n mod p) mod m, and n mod p is small enough to iterate.
